queries: site.metr.org March 2025 measuring AI ability complete long tasks doubling seven months

sources_considered.why: Independent benchmark organizer's dated evaluation, including methodology and limitations.
Version-pinned independent research provides corroborating evidence of capability progress through early 2025.
Read for methodological checks; the version-pinned paper was preferred because the webpage contains later chart updates.
Read as a check on remaining software-task limitations. It measures a different task set and does not provide a comparable before-and-after test of this forecast.

evidence_items.explanation: ARC Prize reports 75.7% and 87.5% for the o3 preview configurations and contrasts these with GPT-4o's 5% performance in 2024. The evaluator describes a substantial advance, while disclosing benchmark-specific training and increased inference computation.

Independent comparisons extending through early 2025 find substantial growth in the human-duration tasks agents can complete at 50% success. This corroborates progress beyond a single ARC evaluation, although the task sample and success threshold limit generalization.
Material qualification: the same evaluator identifies continuing basic failures. Substantial measured improvement does not establish AGI or eliminate reliability limitations.

unresolved_gaps: Comprehensive development costs for the evaluated improvements are not established.
ARC's tested preview received benchmark-specific training and differs from the subsequently released o3.
The evidence does not measure every generative AI domain or establish dependable performance across ordinary work.
